subject: Security exhibit redlines & audit-notice window — evidence ownership clarification
messages:
From: Sarah Wright <sarah.wright@arborhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: contracts@arborhealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit redlines and audit-notice window

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for sending the draft MSA + order form. Legal at ArborHealth attached a marked-up security exhibit (attached). A few items we want to clarify before legal signs off:

1) Pen-test notice / inspection window: we need a minimum of 21 business days notice for in-person or scoped penetration tests (to coordinate internal controls).
2) Evidence cadence: we prefer monthly evidence snapshots for the SOC 2 controls referenced in the exhibit; please confirm what Redwood can commit to (format and delivery channel).
3) Audit scope carveouts: we redlined an explicit carveout for third-party subprocessors with their own SOC 2 / attestations — we expect Redwood to provide a list of those and attestations on request.
4) Retention & redaction: added language asking for a sample evidence retention policy and redaction commitments for customer-specific logs.

Would appreciate a short runnable proposal from your side that maps each redline to an owner and a realistic timeline. We are on a tight procurement calendar and need to close legal review by 2027-07-07 to hit our internal renewal window.

Attachments: arbor_exhibit_redline.pdf (redlines)

Best,
Sarah Wright
Legal Counsel, ArborHealth
+sarah.wright@arborhealth.com
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com>

Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit redlines and audit-notice window

Sarah —

Thanks for the markup and the clear asks. I pulled together an operational response below + attached a redlines_response_v1.docx that maps each numbered item to an internal owner and target date. High level answers first, then a short proposed clause for the pen-test notice window you can consider.

High level commitments we can make now:
- Pen-test notice: Redwood can commit to a 10 business day standard notice for remote tests and a 15 business day notice for on-site or staging-access tests. For customers that require longer (e.g., 21 business days), we can accept that as a negotiated order-form exception.
- Evidence cadence: We can provide monthly SOC2 evidence snapshots (PDF + index) delivered to a secure shared Drive link. For higher-frequency needs we can agree to weekly logs exports for specific SAML/audit events — those would be scoped in the order form.
- Subprocessor attestations: We will provide a current list of subprocessors and their latest attestation links within 5 business days of contract execution; we can add a one-time attestation delivery line item to the order form.
- Retention & redaction: We propose the attached evidence runbook (Drive link) as the canonical retention policy for third-party review; Redwood will redact customer-identifying data from sampling exports by default.

Proposed pen-test notice clause (draft):
"Customer shall provide Redwood with written notice of intended penetration testing no less than ten (10) business days for remote testing and fifteen (15) business days for on-site testing. Timbered exceptions with customer-specific order-form language may extend notice to twenty-one (21) business days where required by customer policy"

Next steps we suggest:
- Confirm whether ArborHealth can accept the 10/15 business day split or if 21 is a strict mandatory requirement tied to procurement.
- If 21 days is mandatory, we will flag as an order-form exception and request a Committed Capacity/Operational SLA carveout for staging access.
- If acceptable, we'll finalize language and produce a short evidence-ownership matrix (names + SLAs) and route for legal redline acceptance.

Attachments: redlines_response_v1.docx; pen_test_scope.xlsx

Thanks — looping Dylan & Priyom to assign owners on ops/legal side.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Legal Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood-inference.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood-inference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit redlines and audit-notice window

Quick internal note — I reviewed Kimberly's draft responses. Two operational asks before we send final back to ArborHealth:

1) Escrow / evidence escrow: Arbor flagged retention and redaction. Legal should avoid open-ended escrow commitments. Suggest we offer a 90-day evidence snapshot retention for audit purposes and point them to our current SOC2 evidence portal.
2) Pen-test notice: 21 business days seems heavy for remote tests. If Arbor insists, we should require a scoped staging window and confirm that Redwood may schedule around existing customer testing. Add a short schedule: 21 business days accepted only for on-site or full-scope inspections.

If everyone agrees, I'll tidy up the order-form exception language and provide a short redline (10–15 vs 21 split) that legal can attach.

— Priyom
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Kimberly / team —

- Share the evidence ownership matrix (who on Redwood is responsible for each control area + expected delivery SLA).
